title: SET Bias Training Taxonomy for AI Implementation
purpose: Detect and contextualize bias indicators in student evaluations of teaching for human review.

bias_types.name: Direct Identity Bias
bias_types.definition: Explicit or coded identity-based language targeting personality, appearance, authority, accent, gender, sexuality, race, culture, or legitimacy.

bias_types.name: Proxy Bias / Pedagogical Dissatisfaction
bias_types.definition: Pedagogically framed complaints that may be valid but can be contaminated by identity bias, grade dissatisfaction, and credibility inversion.
bias_types.default_action: Require context, corroboration, comparator data, and clustering analysis.

bias_types.name: Stigmatized Identity Bias
bias_types.definition: Bias rooted in stereotypes attached to a specific national origin, ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, or gender identity.
bias_types.default_action: Flag for trained human review; use identity-specific training data only when identity context is supplied.

bias_types.name: Deliberate Defamation / Harassment
bias_types.definition: Targeted harassment, threats, false factual claims, coordinated reputational attacks, unadjudicated misconduct allegations, or abusive identity content.
bias_types.default_action: Escalate immediately; do not use in personnel summaries pending protective review.

categories.name: Personality & Temperament
categories.definition: Affective or temperamental descriptions that displace attention from pedagogy to the instructor's personality, authority, or emotional presentation.
signals: has a chip on their shoulder
categories.ai_action: Flag for bias review; look for tone-policing, gendered/racialized stereotypes, and clustering with other identity-coded terms.

categories.name: Authority & Competence Challenges
categories.definition: Challenges to credentials, expertise, preparedness, or authority that can reflect a presumption of incompetence.
signals: students knew more than the professor
categories.ai_action: Flag and require corroboration from peer review, teaching materials, and credentials before treating as a pedagogical fact.

categories.name: Accent & Language Bias
categories.definition: Language that evaluates speech, accent, perceived nativeness, or English ability against an implicit native-English norm.
signals: needs to work on their English
English is not their first language
categories.ai_action: Flag explicit language-bias indicators; separate actual accessibility issues from identity-coded judgments through independent observation.

categories.name: Relatability & Fit
categories.definition: Comments suggesting the instructor does not belong, does not fit, or fails an unstated norm of what a professor should look or sound like.
signals: not the type of professor I expected
feels like they're from a different world
categories.ai_action: Flag as possible fit/forever-foreigner language, especially when unsupported by specific teaching evidence.

categories.name: Gendered Language Patterns
categories.definition: Terms disproportionately applied to women faculty around warmth, assertiveness, appearance, emotion, and professionalism.
categories.ai_action: Flag gendered descriptors and double-bind constructions; compare against language used for male peers.

categories.name: Racialized Language Patterns
categories.definition: Language that racializes authority, affect, threat, foreignness, or perceived difference.
categories.ai_action: Flag for racialized bias review and check whether discomfort with course content is being displaced onto the instructor.

categories.name: Bias Claims Turned Outward
categories.definition: Claims that the instructor is biased, political, or agenda-driven, especially when students' discomfort with material is reframed as instructor misconduct.
signals: grades based on whether you agree
categories.ai_action: Flag; distinguish legitimate content-balance issues from majority-discomfort narratives and grade retaliation.

categories.name: Course Content Complaints as Proxy Bias
categories.definition: Complaints about course subject matter that implicitly challenge the instructor's legitimacy or the legitimacy of identity-related content.
signals: turned every topic into a race/gender issue
not relevant to the subject matter
categories.ai_action: Flag when content complaints target equity topics or the instructor's right to teach them; compare syllabus learning objectives.

categories.name: Pedagogical Complaints as Proxy Bias
categories.definition: Neutral-sounding complaints about grading, feedback, workload, rubrics, course structure, LMS use, due dates, and instructional clarity that may be contaminated by identity bias.
signals: I never know what they want
my grade doesn't reflect my effort
exams don't reflect what we studied
course is all over the place
categories.ai_action: Do not treat as automatically biased or automatically valid; require context, clustering, comparator data, and independent corroboration.

categories.name: Double-Bind of Rigor
categories.definition: A no-win pattern in which high standards are punished as unfair, while accessible courses are dismissed as insufficiently rigorous.
signals: penalizes students for not being perfect
the book was great, the professor not so much
categories.ai_action: Detect contradictory complaint clusters; compare grade distributions and follow-on learning evidence.

categories.name: Structural & Tonal Tropes
categories.definition: Common trope families such as tone policing, angry Black woman/Sapphire trope, model-minority inversion, authority challenge, double bind, emotional labor expectations, and guilt narrative.
signals: made me feel bad about being [identity]
categories.ai_action: Classify trope family; evaluate intersectional compounding and specific protected review needs.

categories.name: Bias Against LGBTQ+ Faculty
categories.definition: Bias triggered by LGBTQ+ disclosure or perceived identity, including political-agenda accusations, credibility challenges, heteronormative content distortion, misgendering, and discomfort framed as harm.
signals: made the class about their personal life
not qualified to teach this objectively
the personal stuff didn't belong in class
made me feel judged for being straight/Christian/traditional
categories.ai_action: Flag disclosure-sensitive patterns; treat deliberate misgendering or identity abuse as escalation content.

categories.name: Stigmatized Ethnic & National Identity Bias
categories.definition: Bias tied to the specific social meanings attached to a national origin, ethnicity, religion, or cultural group, including disgust-organized stigma and forever-foreigner language.
signals: very different from what I'm used to
categories.ai_action: Use only human-supplied identity context; train identity-specific stigma detectors and require careful human review.

categories.name: Deliberate Defamation, Harassment & Weaponization
categories.definition: Targeted harassment, fabricated accusations, unadjudicated misconduct claims, threats, explicit abuse, coordinated attacks, and grade-retaliation defamation.
categories.ai_action: Escalate immediately; exclude from personnel-file summaries pending protective review; do not present as formative feedback.

categories.name: Absence of Positive Language
categories.definition: A comparative signal in which positive intellectual descriptors appear less often for minoritized faculty than for comparable peers.
categories.ai_action: Use comparative corpus analysis, not single-comment judgment; evaluate positive-term rates across instructors and courses.

categories.name: Credibility Inversion
categories.definition: Negative pedagogical feedback is treated as actionable even when it contradicts documented faculty expertise, years of experience, peer observations, or scholarly record.
signals: confusing explanations despite extensive teaching record
no clear rubric despite documented rubrics
complaints increase over time despite growing experience
categories.ai_action: Run corroboration-gap test; weigh credentials, teaching portfolio, peer observation, temporal stability, and comparator data before classification.

categories.name: Grade Distributions as SET Context
categories.definition: Grade distributions contextualize SET credibility because grades and grade satisfaction shape ratings and complaint patterns.
signals: same grades but worse SETs than comparator
categories.ai_action: Integrate mean GPA, DFW, withdrawals, departmental norms, comparator sections, and follow-on course outcomes before interpreting SETs.

workflow: Normalize comment text, preserve original wording, and assign a stable comment_id.
Detect explicit Type 4 escalation content first: threats, harassment, unadjudicated misconduct allegations, identity abuse, deliberate misgendering, coordinated attacks, or false factual claims.
Detect Type 1 and Type 3 identity-coded indicators using the taxonomy and lexicon.
Detect Type 2 proxy indicators, but mark them as context-dependent rather than automatically biased.
Cluster indicators within a comment and across comments in the same course, term, instructor, and assessment event.

Integrate contextual evidence: grade distribution, DFW, expected grade distribution, timing of evaluation, course level, response rate, peer observation, teaching portfolio, rubrics, LMS logs, and comparator sections.
Apply the grade-distribution matrix and credibility-inversion/corroboration tests.
Generate a structured JSON finding with evidence spans, category labels, confidence, recommended review pathway, and required corroboration.
Never infer instructor protected identity. Use only user- or institution-supplied context, and never make a final personnel judgment automatically.

grade_set_credibility_matrix.ai_flag: Require independent corroboration before treating as actionable.

grade_set_credibility_matrix.interpretation: Rigor may be valued or socially protected
grade_set_credibility_matrix.ai_flag: No automatic bias flag; consider follow-on performance.

grade_set_credibility_matrix.interpretation: Identity-based bias not explained by grade dissatisfaction
grade_set_credibility_matrix.ai_flag: High-probability Type 1 or Type 3 review flag.

grade_set_credibility_matrix.interpretation: Possible genuine effectiveness or strategic grade leniency

safeguards: Flag for review; do not make final personnel judgments automatically.
Do not infer protected identities; use authorized supplied metadata only.
Treat Type 2 pedagogical complaints as context-dependent until corroborated.
Escalate Type 4 content outside ordinary SET review and do not include in personnel summaries pending protective review.
Use grade distributions, comparator sections, peer review, teaching portfolios, and follow-on learning where available.
